advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Escape or reject paths containing quote/backslash characters before embedding them in the Seatbelt profile string.
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py build_seatbelt_profile: `lines.append(f'  (subpath "{Path(path).resolve()}")')`
No quoting/escaping of the interpolated path is applied before embedding it in the Seatbelt profile string
advisory.finding: `build_seatbelt_profile` interpolates resolved paths directly into a quoted S-expression (`(subpath "{path}")`) with no escaping. A path containing a double-quote or backslash produces a malformed profile; sandbox-exec would reject or misparse it, and depending on failure mode the deny rule could be silently dropped.
scenarios: A repo checkout path or venv prefix containing a `"` character (unusual but possible on macOS) yields a broken profile

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/mutation-testing.md 'Local use' to state that `run`/`smoke` require an OS sandbox mechanism (`bwrap` on Linux, `sandbox-exec` on macOS) or abort, and note the `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED` override.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py:591-607 wraps both execute_shard subprocesses via `mutation_sandbox.wrap(...)`
scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:99-116 `wrap` raises `SandboxUnavailable` when `probe()` is None and the opt-out is unset ('the caller must abort rather than run unsandboxed')
scripts/mutation_gate.py:720-721 the `run`/`smoke` path invokes execute_shard
docs/mutation-testing.md:116-126 'Local use' documents `python scripts/mutation_gate.py run`/`smoke` with no mention of a sandbox mechanism or the abort/override
docs/README.md:73 lists mutation-testing.md as the maintained owner of the mutation testing workflow
advisory.finding: docs/mutation-testing.md 'Local use' instructs contributors to run `scripts/mutation_gate.py run`/`smoke`, but those commands now abort with SandboxUnavailable when no OS sandbox (`bwrap`/`sandbox-exec`) is installed, and the section does not state that prerequisite or the `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED` override.
scenarios: A Linux contributor without bwrap runs the documented `mutation_gate.py run` command and hits an unexplained SandboxUnavailable abort
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/mutation-testing.md 'Local use' (around lines 116-126), add that `run`/`smoke` execute shard tests inside an OS sandbox and abort when none is available, pointing to the `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED` override documented in docs/local-dev-env.md.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the sandbox enforcement tests execute on a gating lane: install bubblewrap in the mutation/test job (or add a `platform_compat`-marked enforcement case on the macOS gate) so at least one 'write-outside-allow-list-is-denied' assertion runs pre-merge.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:22 `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`
tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:38-41 `live = pytest.mark.skipif(sb.probe() is None, reason="no OS sandbox mechanism on this host (sandbox-exec or bwrap)")`

test file docstring lines 7-9: 'These tests observe **enforcement**... Asserting the wrapper argv alone would pass against a sandbox that silently denies nothing — which is the exact failure mode the fail-closed design exists to prevent.'
search_files for `bubblewrap`/`bwrap` shows no `apt install`/setup step in any workflow — bwrap is installed nowhere, so probe() is None on every Linux runner
_build-and-test.yml:658 macOS cell selects `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS: ... 'platform_compat and not external'`, which excludes the `unit`-marked sandbox tests

ABSENCE rationale: the only lane where sandbox-exec exists AND the full suite runs is sweep-macos-full (test.yml:363-386), gated on `github.event_name == 'schedule' || workflow_dispatch` — non-blocking
advisory.finding: The load-bearing sandbox ENFORCEMENT tests never run on any gating CI lane. They carry both `@live` (skipif sb.probe() is None) and `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`. On the Linux gate cells bwrap/bubblewrap is installed by no workflow, so probe() returns None and every @live test skips; on the macOS gate cell sandbox-exec exists but the `test` matrix selects only `platform_compat and not external` marks, and these tests are `unit`-marked, so they are never collected there either. The enforcement assertions run only on `sweep-macos-full`, which is schedule/workflow_dispatch-only and casts no Verified vote. The one behavior this diff exists to guarantee — that a write outside the allow-list is denied — is therefore verified on no blocking lane.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap` to the Linux test job (and/or the _mutation.yml mutation job) so probe() resolves bwrap and the @live enforcement tests run on the gate; alternatively mark the enforcement tests `platform_compat` so the macOS gate cell selects them.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a construction test for build_seatbelt_profile asserting the emitted profile contains `(deny file-write*)` and a `(subpath "...")` re-permit for each allow-list path (runs on every OS, unlike the @live enforcement path).
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:73-92 `build_seatbelt_profile` emits `(deny file-write*)` then `(allow file-write* (subpath ...))`
search_files `build_seatbelt_profile` returns only the definition and its one internal call site (line 135); no test references it
Named violating input: `build_seatbelt_profile([Path('/tmp/scratch')])` — no test asserts `(deny file-write*)` appears in the returned string nor that the resolved subpath is re-permitted
The unit-marked mechanism tests (test_bwrap_argv_..., test_probe_...) cover bwrap and probe but never the Seatbelt profile text
advisory.finding: build_seatbelt_profile (added, scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:73-92) has no unit test asserting its output. Its only exercise is through the `@live` enforcement tests on macOS, which — per the finding above — run on no gating lane. Nothing asserts the generated profile contains the `(deny file-write*)` directive or re-permits the allow-list subpaths, so a mutation that drops the deny line (yielding an allow-all profile) is undetectable everywhere the tests actually run.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `def test_seatbelt_profile_denies_writes_then_repermits_allowlist(): p = sb.build_seatbelt_profile([Path('/tmp/scratch')]); assert '(deny file-write*)' in p; assert 'scratch' in p` — a pure-string assertion with no host dependency.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the bwrap /dev binding (e.g. `--dev /dev` to create a minimal device set) instead of `--dev-bind /dev /dev` so Linux matches Seatbelt's device write-deny.
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:97 `out = ["bwrap", "--ro-bind", "/", "/", "--dev-bind", "/dev", "/dev", "--proc", "/proc"]`
Seatbelt profile only allows device writes to `/dev/null`, `/dev/stdout`, `/dev/stderr`, `/dev/fd` (scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:85-88)
`--dev-bind` mounts the host /dev read-write inside the sandbox, exposing all device nodes for writing on Linux only
advisory.finding: The Linux bwrap wrapper binds all of /dev writable via `--dev-bind /dev /dev`, while the macOS Seatbelt profile only re-permits four narrow device paths (/dev/null,/dev/stdout,/dev/stderr,/dev/fd). A mutant that reaches a write to a real device node (e.g. a block device) is denied on macOS but permitted on Linux, so the two platforms do not enforce the same write-deny invariant the sandbox exists to guarantee.
scenarios: A destructive mutant on a Linux host writes to a device node under /dev that the equivalent macOS run would deny

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict the sandbox write allow-list to the scratch/basetemp only (or mount the venv read-only) so a mutant cannot write executable code into site-packages that later un-sandboxed steps run.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py:591 `sandbox_allow = (root, basetemp, Path(sys.prefix))`
scripts/mutation_gate.py:618-635 `mutmut results` and `mutmut show` run via `_run(...)` with no `mutation_sandbox.wrap(...)`
The whole venv (site-packages) is a writable allow-list subpath, and subsequent un-sandboxed invocations import from it
advisory.finding: The sandbox allow-list includes `Path(sys.prefix)` (the venv), making site-packages writable inside the sandbox. Because reporting subprocesses (`mutmut results`/`show`) and later gate phases run un-sandboxed, a mutant that writes executable code into site-packages under the sandbox can have it executed later outside the sandbox — a persistence/escape path past the write-deny boundary.
scenarios: A mutant under `mutmut run` writes into a site-packages module; a later un-sandboxed `mutmut show`/`results` (or a subsequent pytest) imports and executes it outside the sandbox

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Create `basetemp` (root/.mutation-pytest) before calling `mutation_sandbox.wrap`, or drop it from the allow-list since it is already under `root` which is bound writable.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py:573: `basetemp = root / ".mutation-pytest"`
scripts/mutation_gate.py:591: `sandbox_allow = (root, basetemp, Path(sys.prefix))`
`_prepare_config` (mutation_gate.py:556-560) only writes pyproject.toml and does not create basetemp; pytest creates it via --basetemp at run time
search for `.mutation-pytest` returns only the definition at line 573 — nothing creates the directory before wrap
scripts/mutation_sandbox.py `_bwrap_argv`: `out += ["--bind", resolved, resolved]` — bwrap requires the bind source to already exist on the host
blocking.finding: The bwrap sandbox binds `basetemp` (root/.mutation-pytest), but that directory is never created before `mutation_sandbox.wrap` is invoked on the baseline pytest. bwrap's `--bind SRC DEST` requires SRC to exist on the host; binding a non-existent path makes bwrap exit non-zero at startup, so the baseline pytest run fails on Linux before pytest ever runs.
scenarios: Linux host with bwrap and no pre-existing root/.mutation-pytest — the first (baseline pytest) sandboxed subprocess fails to launch
blocking.suggested_fix: Call `basetemp.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` in execute_shard before building `sandbox_allow`, or remove `basetemp` from `sandbox_allow` since it lives under `root` (already writable) — but note the Seatbelt subpath also silently no-ops on a missing path while bwrap hard-fails, so mkdir is the consistent fix.
